title: CRLR/593/2022 of HIMANSHU SANWAL Vs STATE OF UTTARAKHAND

paras.text:
HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Criminal Revision No.593 of 2022
Himanshu Sanwal ...Revisionist
Versus

State of Uttarakhand ...Respondent
Present:-
Mr. Abhishek Joshi, Advocate for the revisionist.
 Mr. Pratiroop Pande, A.G.A. for the State.
Hon'ble Ravindra Maithani, J. (Oral)
 The challenge in this revision is made to the order
dated 02.09.2022, passed in the bail application, State Vs.
Child in Conflict with Law ("the CIL"), by the Juvenile
Justice Board ("the JJ Board"), Nainital, by which the bail
application of the CIL has been rejected. Order dated
08.09.2022, passed in Criminal Appeal No. 08 of 2022,
Himanshu Sanwal Vs. State, by the Special Judge
(POCSO)/Additional Sessions Judge, Nainital, has also been
challenged, whereby the bail rejection order of the JJ Board
has been upheld. The revisionist is the CIL. He also seeks
bail.
2. Heard learned counsel for the parties and
perused the record.
3. Learned counsel for the CIL would submit that
the CIL is just 15 years of age. He was in relationship with

2
the victim. The victim is also minor. The applicant is a
student. He is studying in class Xth. There is a family to look
after him. There is nothing adverse in the report of the
Probation Officer.
4. According to the FIR, one day the victim revealed
to her mother that the CIL established physical relations
with her. The record reveals that the victim never raised any
alarm.
5. Learned State counsel admits the factual
position. He would submit that the Probation Officer's report
is not adverse in the CIL.
6. In the matters of CIL, bail is a rule irrespective of
the offence being classified as bailable or non-bailable. But,
the only rider is proviso to Section 12 (1) of the Juvenile
Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015 ("the
Act"). In case release of the CIL brings him into association
to any known criminal or may cause him to moral, physical
or psychological danger or it may defeat the ends of justice,
only in such cases, bail may be denied.
7. One of the principles that governs the provisions
of the Act are given under Section 3 of the Act. According to
it, the primary responsibility of care, nurturing and

3
protection of the child is that of the biological family of the
CIL.
8. The Probation Officer's report reveals that the CIL
has a family to look after him.
9. Having considered the entirety of facts, this Court
is of the view that it is the case in which the provisions of
Section 12 (1) of the Act is not applicable. Accordingly, the
revision deserves to be allowed.
10. The revision is allowed. The impugned orders are
set aside.
11. The CIL be given into the custody of his father
subject to production of two reliable sureties by him. The
father of the CIL shall also give an undertaking that he shall
take care of the CIL and shall not allow him to contact any
of the witnesses or their family members. The father of the
CIL shall also undertake that he shall also not contact
either the witnesses or any of their family members.
 (Ravindra Maithani, J.)
 13.01.2023
Kaushal
